meta.description: Blind set 2: 35 edge cases (all 22 categories of set 1, new personas and scenarios) + 15 routine reports. Synthetic only. Built to evaluate the frozen flag layer (git tag flag-layer-final). Do not run any parser on this file before the labels in data/blind2_review.csv are reviewed by the author.

reports.persona: 76-year-old retired pastor who loves to talk
reports.scenario_hint: About 200 words about the church bake sale, the choir and his neighbour's cat; buried in the middle: vomited twice yesterday evening.
reports.text: Well hey there, it is a peculiar Thursday evening for a man who has been sitting in his armchair reading the Good News, but my mind is racing like a stallion. I have to tell you, the bake sale at Grace Fellowship last Saturday was an absolute triumph, or so the deacons insisted, despite my being unable to lift nearly anything off the table. Sister Mary’s lemon bars were divine, I assure you, purely from a theological perspective on sweet things. The choir practice afterward was loud, specifically the baritones, as usual, and I stood there nodding along though my legs felt like wet noodles. That brought me to my neighbor Jenkins’ cat, who decided to get underfoot right in the middle of the hymn, causing quite a distraction that bordered on spiritual chaos. I am telling you this because I am rambling, as is my custom, and I am still tired as a mule. But right in the middle of all that church business, I have to mention that I vomited twice yesterday evening, around seven o’clock, which was a bit of a letdown for the evening. Otherwise, the cat is back to sleeping on the porch and I am just trying to be still, thank God, with the phone signaling for this update. Peace be with whoever reads this, and may your coffee be hot and your days be long, but for now, I am just a tired old pastor trying to rest his eyes and his stomach, so I shall sign off with a blessing and a yawn.
